nodes.content: Develop a shared-control robot that distinguishes human intent changes from reactions to its assistance during collaborative object transport.
requirements: Achieve intent-change F1 ≥0.85 for unseen partners when robot assistance itself induces human corrections.
Reduce unnecessary control overrides by 30% versus a fixed-assistance baseline without increasing peak interaction forces.

nodes.content: Train partner-invariant, robot-action-conditioned human-response forecasts; classify persistent unexplained motion as intent change, then gate peak-force-constrained control overrides.
Can robot-action-conditioned motion forecasts separate assistance-induced corrections from genuine intent changes for unseen partners?
With assistance-induced corrections, action-conditioned residuals will achieve unseen-partner intent-change F1 ≥0.85, at least 0.10 above action-blind residuals.
Randomize assistance pulses during transport, annotate goal changes, train action-conditioned and action-blind forecasters, and compare unseen-partner intent-change F1.
Collect TransportPulse-24: 24 partners carry trays under randomized assistance pulses and cued, annotated destination changes; reserve six unseen partners.
TransportPulse-24 dataset with synchronized human motion, robot commands, interaction forces, intent-change labels, and an 18-train/6-unseen-partner split.
Audit TransportPulse-24 labels and partner splits, then benchmark action-conditioned versus action-blind forecasters on six unseen partners' intent-change F1.
TransportPulse-24 audit passed; unseen-partner intent-change F1 was 0.78 action-conditioned versus 0.74 action-blind, below both predicted thresholds.
Defer deploying action-conditioned residual gating; its 0.78 unseen-partner F1 misses 0.85, warranting analysis of assistance-response timing.
Train lag-aware action-conditioned and action-blind forecasters on TransportPulse-24; compare intent-change F1 for six unseen partners after assistance pulses.
Lag-aware action conditioning raised unseen-partner intent-change F1 from 0.78 to 0.87 on TransportPulse-24; action-blind scored 0.74.
What residual-persistence window suppresses assistance-induced overrides without delaying genuine destination changes or raising peak interaction forces?
Sweep 100–500-ms residual-persistence windows across six unseen partners; compare unnecessary overrides, intent latency, and peak forces against fixed assistance.
At 300 ms, unnecessary overrides fell 34%; peak force was 24 versus 25 N under fixed assistance.
PersistenceSweep-v1 contains per-window override rates, intent latencies, peak forces, and the 300-ms gating configuration.
Integrate 300-ms residual-persistence gating with lag-aware intent estimates and a 25-N force cap for adaptive transport assistance.
Run held-out-partner trials of lag-aware 300-ms gating versus fixed assistance; measure intent-change F1, unnecessary overrides, and peak forces.
Using PersistenceSweep-v1, run eight-new-partner crossover trials comparing integrated gating with fixed assistance on intent-change F1, unnecessary overrides, and peak forces.
Eight-partner crossover: intent-change F1 0.83; unnecessary overrides fell 24%; peak interaction force reached 29 versus fixed assistance’s 25 N.
Are 29-N interaction-force peaks driven by human counterforces during delayed intent recognition despite the controller’s 25-N cap?
Force peaks above 25 N coincide with human counterforces during the 300-ms gating delay after destination changes.
Align eight-partner crossover force traces to destination-change cues; test whether >25-N peaks coincide with counterforces during 300-ms gating delays.
In crossover traces, 82% of >25-N peaks coincided with opposing human forces within 300 ms of cued destination changes.
Defer deployment; revise gating with counterforce-triggered assistance release after 0.83 F1, 24% override reduction, and counterforce-linked 29-N peaks.
Implement counterforce-triggered assistance release; compare >25-N peaks during delayed, counterforce-positive destination changes against prior gating.
Lag-aware, action-conditioned forecasts with counterforce-triggered release will yield unseen-partner intent-change F1 ≥0.85 without >25-N force peaks.
Train on TransportPulse-24; test counterforce-release gating with eight new partners under assistance pulses, measuring intent-change F1 and peak force.
Release trials with eight unseen partners achieved intent-change F1 0.86, 32% fewer overrides versus fixed assistance, and 25-N peak force.
Use calibrated dual-hypothesis filtering to distinguish intent changes from assistance reactions and soften robot authority under uncertainty.
At what dual-hypothesis posterior confidence should robot authority soften during ambiguous counterforces without delaying genuine destination changes?
Halving authority at intent-change posteriors 0.35–0.65 will retain F1 ≥0.85, ≥30% fewer overrides versus fixed assistance, and ≤25-N peaks.
Run ten-new-partner crossover trials comparing 0.35–0.65 posterior authority halving against release-only and fixed assistance; measure F1, overrides, peak force.
Ten-partner crossover: authority halving scored F1 0.82, 35% fewer overrides than fixed assistance, and 24-N peaks.
Use PersistenceSweep-v1 to select low-force windows; compare 0.35–0.65 authority halving with fixed assistance on unseen-partner F1, overrides, and force.
On six TransportPulse-24 held-out partners, window-selected authority halving reached F1 0.86, 33% fewer overrides than fixed assistance, and 24-N peaks.
Does window selection overfit TransportPulse-24, explaining F1 0.86 on its held-out partners versus 0.82 on ten new partners?
Partner-specific counterforce timing causes the F1 gap: recalibrating posterior windows on early unlabeled interactions will restore new-partner F1 ≥0.85.
Compare fixed and early-interaction-calibrated posterior windows on untouched partners, stratifying intent-change F1 by measured counterforce delay.
Using both prior F1 results, test fixed versus early-interaction-calibrated windows on untouched partners, stratifying F1 by counterforce delay.
CalibrationAudit-v1 contains untouched-partner fixed-versus-calibrated F1 comparisons, counterforce-delay strata, and a label-free early-interaction calibration protocol.
Replicate CalibrationAudit-v1’s label-free calibration on twelve additional partners; compare fixed versus calibrated intent-change F1 across counterforce-delay strata.
Across twelve additional partners, calibration raised intent-change F1 from 0.81 to 0.86; long-delay cases improved from 0.76 to 0.85.
Combine label-free partner-calibrated intent filtering with counterforce-triggered assistance release and force-limited authority during ambiguous transport corrections.
Preregister untouched-partner crossover trials comparing calibrated release-and-authority control with fixed assistance on F1, override reduction, and peak force.
Apply CalibrationAudit-v1’s label-free protocol in 16-partner crossover trials; compare combined control against fixed assistance on F1, overrides, peak force.
Sixteen-partner crossover: combined control achieved intent-change F1 0.87, 36% fewer unnecessary overrides than fixed assistance, and 24-N peak force.
Replicate the 16-partner crossover on 20 untouched partners, comparing intent-change F1, override reduction, and peak force against fixed assistance.
ReplicationReport-v1 contains 20 untouched partners’ intent-change F1, override rates, and peak-force comparisons against fixed assistance.
Can partner-calibrated intent posteriors coordinate counterforce release and reduced authority without delaying genuine destination changes?
Partner-calibrated release-and-authority control will achieve F1 ≥0.85, ≥30% fewer overrides, ≤25-N peaks, and ≤200-ms destination-change latency.
Time-stamp destination cues in new-partner crossover trials; compare combined control with fixed assistance on latency, F1, overrides, and force.
Using TransportPulse-24 and ReplicationReport-v1, compare release-only, calibrated combined, and fixed assistance on new partners’ F1, overrides, force, and latency.
New-partner release-only: F1 0.86, 25-N peak; combined: F1 0.87, overrides down 34% versus fixed, 24-N peak, 260-ms latency.
Using PersistenceSweep-v1 and ReplicationReport-v1, compare 150–250-ms combined-control gates with fixed assistance on new-partner F1, overrides, force, and latency.
At 150-ms gating: latency 190 ms, unseen-partner F1 0.83, overrides down 27% versus fixed assistance, peak force 24 N.
Can earlier release preserve release-only’s 32% override reduction while cutting combined-control latency below 200 ms without 150-ms gating’s F1 loss?
Early counterforce-triggered release with 300-ms intent gating will reach ≤200-ms latency, F1 ≥0.85, ≥30% fewer overrides, and ≤25-N peaks.
Benchmark early-release 300-ms gating against prior combined and 150-ms controllers on unseen-partner latency, F1, overrides, and peak force.
On 12 unseen partners, early release achieved 185-ms latency, F1 0.86, 32% fewer overrides versus fixed assistance, and 24-N peaks.
EarlyRelease-v1 controller integrates 300-ms intent gating, early counterforce-triggered release, partner calibration, and force-limited assistance.
Advance EarlyRelease-v1 to replication: 185-ms latency and 0.86 F1 address prior tradeoffs, with 32% fewer overrides and 24-N peaks.
Extend EarlyRelease-v1 with uncertainty-triggered passive fallback for unfamiliar payload masses and assistance reversals.
When payload mass or assistance direction shifts, does posterior uncertainty identify unreliable intent estimates early enough for passive fallback?
Under mass shifts or assistance reversals, posterior entropy will flag ≥80% of erroneous overrides ≥100 ms early for passive fallback.
Perturb payload mass and reverse assistance during transport; assess entropy warning lead time before erroneous overrides and fallback’s force effect.
Using CalibrationAudit-v1 and EarlyRelease-v1, vary payload mass and reverse assistance; measure entropy-warning lead time, erroneous-override detection, and passive-fallback peak forces.
ShiftStress-v1 contains mass-shift and assistance-reversal traces, entropy warnings, erroneous-override labels, and passive-fallback force measurements.
Audit ShiftStress-v1 timestamps and override labels; compute ≥100-ms-ahead entropy-warning recall and passive-fallback peak forces across both perturbations.
ShiftStress-v1 audit passed; entropy warned ≥100 ms before 83% of erroneous overrides; passive-fallback peak force was 24 N.
Using ShiftStress-v1’s validated 100-ms warnings, compare entropy-triggered fallback with calibrated combined control: F1, overrides, peak force.
ShiftStress-v1: fallback achieved F1 0.86, 32% fewer overrides versus fixed assistance, and 24-N peaks; combined control peaked at 28 N.
Advance EarlyRelease-v1 with conditional fallback, requiring preservation of the 16-partner 0.87-F1 benchmark; early warnings limit shifted-condition peaks to 24 N.
Test conditional-fallback EarlyRelease-v1 on 20 new partners under nominal and ShiftStress-v1 perturbations; compare F1, overrides, and forces with fixed assistance.
FallbackReplication-v1 reports nominal and shifted-condition F1, unnecessary-override reductions, and peak forces for 20 untouched partners versus fixed assistance.
